description: Anchored at the start, anywhere, and the whole string. JavaScript's `test` and `String.match` behave like `search`.
`(?P<name>...)` in Python; `Match.groupdict()` returns the captured groups by name.
In `str` patterns `\d`, `\w`, `\s` and `\b` follow Unicode; use `[0-9]` or `re.ASCII` for ASCII only.
`+` takes as much as possible and gives back on failure; `+?` takes as little as possible. A negated class such as `[^\]]+` avoids both.
Denial of service through backtracking: nested or unbounded quantifiers on almost-matching input take exponential or quadratic time.
`(?>...)` (Python 3.11+): once it matches, the engine never backtracks into it.
